known_limitations: Broadcom Wi-Fi constraint: BCM43684 transceivers lack open-source mac80211 drivers; wireless radios are non-functional under pure OpenWrt.
Ethernet routing, VLAN, and wired packet forwarding function normally, but device acts essentially as a wired-only router.

evidence: Upstream OpenWrt bcm4908 target support present in Git tree

linux_driver.wireless_mac80211: brcmfmac / b43 (Proprietary Broadcom SDK required for full Wi-Fi 6 operation)

chipsets.notes: Powers high-end consumer routers like ASUS GT-AX11000 and Netgear RAX80. While the Linux CPU and DSA Ethernet switch work under OpenWrt bcm4908, the wireless transceivers require closed-source proprietary Broadcom binary blobs ('wl.ko') not redistributable in mainline OpenWrt, leaving wireless non-functional or severely degraded on pure open-source builds.

chipsets.part_number: x86_64 Generic (Intel N100 / J4125 / Core / Xeon)

wireless_subsystem.wi_fi_generation: Varies by M.2 PCIe Wi-Fi card

chipsets.notes: Standard architecture for soft-routers and dedicated firewall appliances (e.g. Protectli Vault, Topton, Qotom, PC Engines APU, generic mini-PCs). Unmatched CPU throughput for complex routing, 10G WireGuard VPN, Suricata IDS, and heavy SQM CAKE traffic shaping.
Cost-effective, highly efficient Wi-Fi 6 SoC prevalent in compact travel routers (e.g. GL-MT3000) and entry-to-midrange wireless access points.

Flagship Wi-Fi 6 router platform featuring dual 2.5G SGMII interfaces, hardware packet processing engine (PPE v2), and Wireless Ethernet Dispatch (WED v2) providing line-rate routing with sub-5% CPU utilization under OpenWrt flow offloading.

State-of-the-art 6nm networking platform engineered for multi-gigabit gateways (Banana Pi BPI-R4). Supports quad 10GbE interfaces (USXGMII) and PCIe 3.0 interfaces for Wi-Fi 7 MLO (Multi-Link Operation).

wireless_subsystem.mimo_capabilities: Varies by companion PCIe RF chip (typically 2x2 or 4x4)

chipsets.notes: The ubiquitous historical workhorse of budget Gigabit OpenWrt routers (e.g. TP-Link Archer C6 v3, Xiaomi Mi Router 4A Gigabit, D-Link DIR-882). Highly mature Linux target with hardware NAT flow offloading.
Highly popular Wave-2 AC chipset (e.g. GL.iNet GL-B1300, Linksys EA8300, ASUS RT-AC58U, Netgear Orbi RBR50). Outstanding open-source driver maturity via ath10k.
High-performance enterprise and prosumer Wi-Fi 6 platform powering routers such as Xiaomi AX9000, GL.iNet GL-AXT1800, and Netgear WAX218. Features dedicated Network Subsystem (NSS) coprocessors.
Mid-tier Wi-Fi 6 chipset powering widespread models like Xiaomi AX1800, Redmi AX5, and GL.iNet Flint (GL-AX1800). Full upstream ath11k driver support.

Dedicated managed switch platform powering 8-port to 24-port Gigabit smart switches (e.g. Zyxel GS1900-8, D-Link DGS-1210). Fully supported via upstream OpenWrt realtek/rtl838x target with Linux DSA switch fabric integration.

wireless_subsystem.wi_fi_generation: Varies by M.2 / PCIe Wi-Fi card

chipsets.notes: Workhorse of modern multi-gigabit SBC routers (e.g. FriendlyElec NanoPi R5S / R5C, Radxa E25). Features native dual PCIe 2.5GbE PHYs (Realtek RTL8125BG) delivering full 2.5 Gbps wire speed under OpenWrt.
